full_judgment:
2. The material facts leading to the instant civil revision are that the petitioner as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 194 of 1979 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla which being transferred to the Court of Subordinate judge Chandpur was renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 against the defendant-opposite parties praying for declaration of title to schedule-1 land to the plaint and for recovery of khas possession of the schedule-2 land to the plaint by evicting the defendant Nos. 2-54. 

 3. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit schedule-1 property to the plaint measuring an area of 1.62 acres of land recorded in CS. Khatian No.141 of Mouza Kaladi, PS Matlab belonged originally to Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury in Hovvla who constructed a Temple in the Suit Plot No. 408 and established the Deity Sree Sree Jagannath Deb Bigraha Thakur there. The Suit Plot No. 403 was fixed for Rath (Chariot) of the Deity adjacent to the temple. There is a tank in the Plot No. 405 which is used for bathing of the Deity and his daily archana. Plot No. 402 is used as a pathway and Plot No. 407 is a garden in the Deity. Raj Kumar Roy gifted the suit land to the plaintiff-Deity on 10th Sraban, 1326 BS by a registered deed of gift and for conducting the entire ceremonies and affairs of the Deity and appointed a committee named `Sushasan Committee' except the daily puja, are held there. Dole Ceremony, Rath Jatra Ceremony, Harinam Sankirtan and Mohautsab etc. There was never any hot on the entire plot No. 402 0.28 decimals of land of the said plot from north to east side is used as hat. On the death of Raj Kumar his sons Lalit Mohan and others became the shebayet of the Deity. At that time Lalit Mahan settled-out 0.04 decimals of land from plot No. 402 with Ramani Chakraborty and thereafter, Ramani Chakraborty gifted that. On behalf of the Deity one disciple of the Deity filed Title Suit No. 145 of 1940 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court; Chandpur against the Shebayet Lalit Kumar Roy Chowdhury and others for declaration that Deity is the "Public Idol" of the Hindu Communities of Matlab Bazar and got decree on 21-2-1941 in terms of solenama and in pursuance of the decree a "Seba Committee" with Aswini Kumar Biswas as the Secretary for the performance of religious ceremony and for administration of the property of the Deity formed and attested record of rights under East Bangal Estate Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was prepared on 15-10-1953 in the name of the Deity for the entire khas land of the Deity. In the said attested khatian 39 decimals of land of plot No. 402 excluding the remaining land of the plot for the hat was correctly recorded along with other land in the name of the Deity. The Secretary, Aswini Kumar Biswas paid rent in respect of the suit land to the Government for 1365 to 1368 BS and got dakhi as. During the Pak Military atrocity in 1971 the apparels of the temple was plundered away and the Hindu people of the area left for India. Taking advantage of the absence of the committee and the Hindu people the concerned officials of the Government by order dated 4-10-1971 most illegally made the entire property of schedule-I khas land of the Government and recorded the same in Khas Khatian No. 1 and started to settle out the said property to different persons illegally. After the liberation of Bangladesh the Seba Committee of the Deity started all out reforms of the temple. But the defendant Nos. 2-54 started to forcibly enter into the suit property illegally and constructed shops therein by dispossession of the plaintiff. The defendants have no right and title to the suit land. In view of the Aforesaid facts and circumstances, the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 5. The case of the defendant Nos. 8, 51, 54 is that the suit land and some other land originally belonged to Raj Kumar Roy who died leaving behind 5 sons namely Lalit Mohan Roy, SUrendra Kumar Roy, Narendra Kumar Roy, Kamini Kumar Roy and Rajendra Kumar Roy Kamini Kumar died leaving behind only son Benode Behari and Rajendra Kumar died leaving behind his daughter Usha Rani. Raj Kumar never gifted the land plot No. 402 to the deity Jagannath Dev and the alleged deed does not cover the land of plot No. 402. Lalit Mohan and others settled out 1.5 decimals of land from plot No. 402 on 5th Baishakh, 1349 BS with these defendants and since then these defendants have been possessing the same. The land of plot No. 402 has been correctly recorded in khas khatian in the name of Government and the rn SDO, Chandpur settled-out the said land with these defendants. 

 11. The case of the defendant Nos.; 12-15, 17, 21, 26, 27, 30-34, 36 and 38 is that the suit plot Nos. 402 and 400 are owned and possessed by. Motlab Masjid Committee: There is a pond in plot No. 405 and water of the said pond is used by the Musallis. The Masjid committee got the said land by purchase froth Maharam Ali by registered kabala. The defendants are tenants of the Masjid committee. The Government has been using the suit land 'except the suit plot No. 402 as land of Toha Bazar from time immemorial. There is a `Alchra' of the Hindu Community in the plot No 404 where the Hindus observe their "puja and religious ceremonies. Except the plot No. 404, no other suit land is Debatar property; as per State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land is the khas land of the Government. 

 13. The case of the defendant-NO.14, is that the said suit land is khas land of the Government and this defendant took settlement of the said land on' 20-11-1970 and has been-possessing the suit land by constructing building and other structures with surrounding wall., The Government settled out some land to the Union Parishad. Ultimately, Hats and Bazar being vested in the Government, the suit land became khas land of the Government. 

 14. The case of the defendant No. 22 is that this defendant took settlement of .03 decimals of land of plot No. 403 from the government by dahila. Thereafter, the Government took that and bazar in khas and this defendant took lease from the government and accordingly, SA Khatian No, 590 has been correctly prepared in their names. 

 19. Mr AB Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate representing the plaintiff petitioner submits that the Courts below by passing the respective judgments and decrees committed error of law in resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice; that as the boundary of the alleged deed of gift dated 30-7-1999 being relayed by an Advocate Commissioner and on relay as the land within the boundary of the deed of gift attracts the suit land, the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the suit land: is not properly identified is not a correct decision; that the finding of the 'appellate' Court below that the suit is not maintainable on the ground that the order of the SDO,. Chandpur dated 4-10-1971 declaring the suit land as khas land of Government stands valid still now. inasmuch as the said order is illegal and void under the President Order No.12 of 1971 is an erroneous finding that the appellate Court below committed an error of law in holding that, the deed of gift dated 30-7-1919 was not acted upon that the Courts below acted on mere surmise and conjecture in passing the-respective judgment and decrees; that the Courts below should have held that the plaintiff has right, title and interest in the entire schedule property. The learned Advocate lastly prays for making the Rule absolute and to set aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

 20. M. Mr Khizir Hayat, the learned Deputy Attorney-General (DAG) representing the opposite parties submits that the appellate Court below rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree; that the suit land is rightly included in the khas khatian in the Government; that by passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court below committed no error of law resulting in any error in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning any failure of justice. The learned DAG lastly submits that there being no merit in the Civil Revision Case, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 21. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties and considered the materials on record. 22. As stated earlier, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 194 of 1979 which on transfer' was renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 for declaration of title in the schedule-1 land to the plaint and for recovery of khas possession in respect of the land of schedule-2 to the plaint. Said suit was dismissed by the trial Court vide he judgment and decree dated 15-4-1999 and 22-4- 1999 respectively. As against the said judgment and decree the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No.23 of 1988 which was disallowed vide the impugned judgment and decree affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 23. On perusal of ,the judgment of the trial Court it is, found that the trial Court dismissed the suit finding that the suit is barred by limitation; that the suit is bad for defect of parties and that without prayer for partition the suit cannot be maintained. On the other hand, the appellate Court below passed the impugned judgment, and decree dated. 15-4-1999 and 22-4-1999 respectively holding that the suit is not barred limitation and that the suit is not bad for default of parties reversing the finding of the trial Court, The Government or the defendants did not raise any objection against the aforesaid finding the appellate Court below and, as such, it is to be taken that the defendants have accepted the said finding of the appellate court below. So, in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, the ambit of the instant revision has become very narrow and in the civil revision case, the point mainly to be decided is whether the suit property is Debottor property on whether the Government has rightly made the property khas land. 

 24. To substantiate his case, the plaintiff filed exhibit-1 the deed of gift dated .30-71 919 executed by Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury exhibit-1/1 kabala dated 15-12-1939 executed by Ramani Mohan Chowdhury favouring Lalit Kumar Roy Chowdhury, ext. 1/2 registered deed dated 15-9-1979 executed by Sree Ramani Mohan Chowdhury favouring the plaintiff. Exhibit-3-3 (Kha) khas, i.e. CS Khatian No.141. Petty khatian No. 141 and Khas khatian No. 1, exhibit-4 series rent receipts in respett of land of the khatian No. 141 for an area of 1.58 acres of land to the Government. The exhibit-1 shows that Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury gifted the suit land to the plaintiff. Exhibit-3 the CS khatian No. 141 which recorded in the name of Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury. Exhibit-3(a), the petty khatian No. 141 stand recorded in the name of the Deity i.e. the plaintiff. Exhibit-3(b) is the khas khatian in the name of the Government. Exhibit-4 series shows that the plaintiff paid rent of 1.58 acres of land. In this case the exhibit-1 i:e. deed of gift dated 304-1999 is not denied by the defendants. The finding of the appellate Court below is that the exhibit-1 deed of gift is not acted upon. The very recording of the suit land in the name of the plaintiff Deity in Ext.3(a) petty khatian, acceptance of rent by Government from the plaintiff by issuing rent-receipts- Exhibit-4-4(a) series manifest that the Exhibit-1- Deed of gift is acted upon and that by accepting rent of the suit land from the plaintiff-Deity, the Government recognized the plaintiff as a tenant under it. Further, after admitting the plaintiff to be a tenant by way of accepting rent from him and recognizing him as a tenant under it, the Government cannot make the suit property a khas land. Section 20(5)(i)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956 puts an embargo upon the Government to make a Debutter, Waqf property to be a Government khas land. In support of the plaintiffs case, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff cited the case of Hindu Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu vs Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property (now vested property), Government of Bangladesh reported in 51 DLR 300 in which case it is held that "Once a property becomes a property of the Deity, which is immortal, it continues to be a property of the Deity for all times to come." 

 25. From the discussion made here above, and so also on observation of the aforesaid case law, this Court is of the opinion that the suit property is a Debutter Property which the Government cannot make Government khas land. 

 26. As to the finding of the trial Court that the suit land is vague and unspecified, it is to be noted here that in. the Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 a local investigation in respect of the', suit property was held to ascertain as to whether the land as described within the boundary of the exhibit-1 tally with the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint. The Advocate Commissioner after holding local investigation submitted report to the effect that the land as described within the boundary of the exhibit-1 'deed of gift is same and identical with the suit property as described in the schedule the plaint. So, the finding 'of the trial Court that the suit land is indefinite and unspecified is not correct. As to the limitation in filing the suit, the plaintiffs’ alleged dispossession from the suit schedule land was in 1972 and the suit was filed in the year 1979. So, the suit being filed within 12 years of the alleged dispossession, the appellate Court below rightly held that the suit is not barred by limitation. It is to be mentioned here that the deed of gift Ext. 1 dated 30-7-1999 was executed after publication of CS record. So, manually the suit land would not be recorded in the name of the plaintiff in the CS khatian. It has already been found that the Petty Khatian No. 141 i.e. Ext. 3(1) was recorded in the name of the plaintiff. From the discussion made here above, this Court finds right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit schedule-1 land and also find that the suit land is not a Government Khas land; that the plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit schedule-2 land by the defendants and that the alleged settlement or lease by the Government to any defendants is illegal and that the deeds leasing out the suit property to the defends are also illegal and void documents. 

 32. The plaintiff Deity is held entitled to get khas possession of the schedule-2 property to the plaint evicting the defendant Nos. 2-54 therefrom by removing all obstructions. The defendant Nos. 2-54 are hereby directed to vacate the schedule-2 land within 90 days from the date of receipt of this judgment removing construction, if any, raised by them in the suit land. The plaintiff is also held entitled to get manse profit of the schedule-2 land during the period of dispossession by the defendant Nos. 2-54.
